identity.title: Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea: waking 1-3 h after sleep with dyspnea relieved by sitting/standing

technique.how: Ask whether the patient wakes from sleep, typically 1-3 hours after lying down, gasping or short of breath and has to sit up, stand or go to a window for relief that takes 10-30 minutes. Ask about wheeze or cough with the episodes and about daytime exertional dyspnoea, orthopnoea and oedema to separate cardiac from asthmatic nocturnal symptoms.
technique.prerequisites: Patient or bed partner able to describe nocturnal episodes.

interpretation.positive_finding: Episodes of waking from sleep with dyspnoea that resolve slowly on sitting or standing indicate redistribution of fluid into the lungs from raised left-sided filling pressure, i.e. decompensated heart failure.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of PND is common in heart failure and provides little reassurance; it should not lower the probability enough to stop the work-up.
interpretation.pitfalls: Nocturnal asthma, COPD with secretions, sleep apnoea, reflux/aspiration and nocturnal angina produce similar waking; 'cardiac asthma' with wheeze is easily mislabelled as asthma. Recall is unreliable and prevalence is low so specificity drives its value.
interpretation.changes_what: PND raises probability of decompensated HF (pooled LR+ ~2.6 in ED) and supports BNP/echo; absence changes little.

estimates.target_condition: Heart failure as cause of acute dyspnoea
estimates.population: Adults presenting to the emergency department with dyspnoea (22 studies pooled)
estimates.reference_standard: Clinical diagnosis of heart failure adjudicated in the primary studies (varied criteria)
estimates.quote: the symptom of paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea (positive LR = 2.6; 95% CI, 1.5-4.5)

estimates.target_condition: Heart failure (cardiac dysfunction at rest on echocardiography)
estimates.population: Portuguese primary care attendees screened by Boston questionnaire and referred for echocardiography (n=1058 assessed); PND sensitivity reported only as <36%
estimates.quote: a history of paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea (LR 35.5), orthopnea (LR 39.1) and breathlessness when walking on the flat (LR 25.8)

estimates.target_condition: Prevalent definite heart failure (composite symptom: orthopnoea OR paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea)
estimates.population: 5,771 community-dwelling adults >=65 years in the Cardiovascular Health Study; 272 with adjudicated definite HF
estimates.reference_standard: Centrally adjudicated definite heart failure (CHS criteria)
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.52/(1-0.83) = 3.06; LR- = (1-0.52)/0.83 = 0.58 from abstract sensitivity 52% and specificity 83%; prevalence = 272/5771
estimates.quote: for either orthopnea or PND were 52% (95% confidence interval [CI] 46% to 58%), 83% (95% CI 82% to 84%)

sources.citation: Wang CS, FitzGerald JM, Schulzer M, Mak E, Ayas NT. Does this dyspneic patient in the emergency department have congestive heart failure? JAMA. 2005;294(15):1944-1956.
Fonseca C, Morais H, Mota T, et al. The diagnosis of heart failure in primary care: value of symptoms and signs. Eur J Heart Fail. 2004;6(6):795-800.

Ekundayo OJ, Howard VJ, Safford MM, et al. Value of orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, and medications in prospective population studies of incident heart failure. Am J Cardiol. 2009;104(2):259-264.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use absence of PND to exclude heart failure; do not label nocturnal wheeze as asthma in an older patient with risk factors for heart failure without checking for congestion.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: PND with chest pain, new oedema or hypoxaemia at rest indicates decompensation that needs same-day assessment rather than outpatient follow-up.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Symptom elicitation is history-dependent with no inter-rater data found; pooled ED sensitivity is low so the finding is present in a minority of heart failure patients.

extraction_notes: Pooled positive LR is quoted from the Wang 2005 abstract; the negative LR and sensitivity/specificity for PND are only in tables that could not be viewed (no open-access full text), so those fields are null and status is partially_quantified. Fonseca 2004 LR 35.5 is a primary-care screening cohort without CI and with sensitivity <36%. Ekundayo 2009 is a composite (orthopnoea OR PND) in a community elderly cohort with LRs computed by this extractor; entered separately, not averaged. Martindale 2016 (PMID 26910112) also pools ED findings but its abstract does not report PND.
